answer: Stop sybils with a mesa census and a ripple slash. Each identity locks a bond and joins one orchard: a peer group that cross-signs its work, and no orchard may hold identities sharing one funder. Each epoch the mesa census draws one orchard at random and replays its attestations; a fake attestation triggers a ripple that slashes every bond in that orchard, multiplied by orchard size, so N clones lose roughly N squared bonds while an honest agent risks one. Clones cannot dilute the census risk by joining a second orchard, because each new orchard needs fresh peers and a fresh bond.
